introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 3 (0750), Paper 3, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Time allowed: three and a quarter hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR QUESTIONS in all. Answer question ONE and three others, choosing ONE question from SECTION B and TWO from SECTION C. Question ONE carries thirty-one marks and the rest carry twenty-three marks each. Only the required number of questions will be marked.

In answering questions on this paper, you are encouraged to refer to your own field and practical work where relevant. Credit will be awarded for such references. Candidates are advised NOT to attempt the questions on field investigations if such an exercise has not been carried out.

Marks will be awarded for well annotated maps and diagrams where these are relevant. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Calculators are allowed. Materials required: Topographic map, Graph Paper and Two outline maps of Cameroon.

Points : Q1 = 31 (5+6+4+4+6+4+2), Q2 à Q7 = 23 chacune (Q2 : 4+2+3+4+5+3+2 ; Q3 : 12+3+5+3 ; Q4 : 5+10+8 ; Q5 : 6+(8+3)+6 ; Q6 : 6+10+7 ; Q7 : 8+6+9), soit 100 points pour les 4 questions à traiter ; aucun écart avec les totaux imprimés. Pour les blocs à plusieurs items (Q1 a, b, c ; Q5 b), `points` de la sous-question est la somme des points imprimés des items.

questions.enonce_markdown: (a) Examine the characteristics of the zonal soil type of the South Cameroon Low Plateau. *(8 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Name of the soil.** The zonal soil of the South Cameroon Plateau, which is under equatorial rain forest, is the **ferrallitic soil (ferralsol)**, the red or yellow tropical soil often called laterite. A zonal soil is one whose characteristics are determined mainly by the climate and the vegetation of the zone.

**Formation (2 marks).** High temperatures and heavy rainfall cause intense chemical weathering; the water percolates downwards and **leaches** the silica and the bases (calcium, magnesium, potassium), and leaves behind the **iron and aluminium oxides** (this is called ferrallitisation or laterisation).

**Characteristics (6 marks).**
1. **Colour:** red to yellowish-red because of the iron oxides. *(1 mark)*
2. **Depth:** very deep, weathered profile, which can reach several metres, with a poorly marked boundary between the horizons. *(1 mark)*
3. **Profile:** a thin, dark humus layer (A horizon) at the surface because the leaf litter decomposes and is recycled quickly; below it a thick, red, clay-rich horizon (B); then a deep weathered rock (C) horizon. *(1 mark)*
4. **Texture and structure:** clayey (mostly kaolinite clay) but stable and porous, well drained and easy to work. *(1 mark)*
5. **Chemistry and fertility:** acid (low pH), low cation exchange capacity and few nutrients; the fertility depends on the **nutrient cycle of the forest**: when the forest is removed the nutrients are lost quickly, the yield falls after two or three seasons, and the farmers have to shift (bush fallow). *(1 mark)*
6. **Hardening and erosion:** if the surface is exposed to the sun and the rain after clearance, the iron-rich layer can harden into a **laterite crust** and the surface soil is eroded easily on slopes. *(1 mark)*

**Conclusion.** The ferrallitic soil is deep and well drained but chemically poor; it supports the dense forest through nutrient cycling but is fragile under farming.

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Briefly explain THREE measures adopted by the government of Cameroon to combat rural exodus. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Answer (three measures, 2 marks each: the measure and its explanation).**
1. **Provision of social amenities and infrastructure in rural areas**: rural electrification, water supply, schools and health centres, and rural roads, which improve the quality of life and make rural areas more attractive. The decentralisation of funds to councils (for example, through the FEICOM council support fund) helps to finance them.
2. **Support to agriculture and rural employment**: credit, subsidised inputs and improved seeds, the creation of agro-industrial and processing units in the villages, and support to young farmers and to cooperatives, so that farming becomes profitable for the youth.
3. **Regional balance and decentralisation**: the creation of growth poles and small towns in the interior (universities, markets, industrial and port projects outside the big cities), and the transfer of competences to councils and regions, so that jobs exist outside Douala and Yaounde.
4. *Other acceptable measures:* land reform and access to land for young people, vocational training, and campaigns to promote rural life.

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) Suggest THREE ways that the government and local population can adopt to manage floods in Cameroon. *(9 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Answer (three ways, 3 marks each: the measure, who does it, and how it works).**
1. **Engineering measures: drainage and flood-control structures** (government). Build and maintain drainage channels, dykes and retention dams, dredge the rivers and the waterways, and enlarge the culverts, so that the flood water is evacuated or stored. For example, the drainage of the large towns such as Douala and the dykes and regulating dams in the Logone and Benue areas of the north.
2. **Land-use planning and regulation** (government with councils). Zone the flood plains and the wetlands as no-build areas, enforce the building regulations, relocate the inhabitants of high-risk areas and provide serviced plots on higher ground; set up flood forecasting and **early warning systems** (the weather services and dam managers inform people before water is released from dams such as Lagdo).
3. **Community actions and environmental management** (local population). Keep the gutters, drains and streams free of **solid waste**, do not build or farm in the waterways, build houses on raised ground, plant trees and grass on the slopes and river banks (**afforestation**) to slow the run-off and reduce erosion and silting, and organise community flood-response and clean-up days.
4. *Other acceptable points:* education and awareness campaigns, flood insurance, emergency relief and shelters, and the construction of flood-resistant houses.
